_comment: Mutation testing — the only mechanical answer to 'can this test actually fail?'.
WHY: a regression test in this repo once passed BOTH before and after the bug was
reintroduced, because it lacked the context that triggered it. Nothing in a normal
toolchain detects that. Stryker rewrites production code one mutant at a time and
re-runs the tests; a SURVIVING mutant is a change to shipped behaviour that no test
objected to — i.e. a test that cannot fail.
SCOPE: deliberately narrow. These are the files where byte-correctness is
load-bearing — if a bit is wrong here, CoH2 rejects or misrenders the output, and no
amount of UI testing catches it. Pointing Stryker at all 126 test files would take
coverageAnalysis 'perTest' is what makes this affordable: Stryker runs only the tests
that actually cover the mutated line, instead of the full 41 s suite per mutant.
_ignoreComment: Stryker copies the project into a sandbox per test-runner process. Without these
exclusions it walks 52,774 files and dies on training/.venv/lib64 — a SYMLINKED
DIRECTORY, which its copyfile call cannot handle (EISDIR).
artifacts/ is ~1.8 GB and release/ holds 150 MB AppImages; copying either four times
over is pure waste. None of this is needed to run the codec tests.
